title: Independent ideas. Extraordinary finds.
intro: A daily selection of independent games and useful Android apps, with original F7 insights and links to their creators.

entries.name: ClassiCube
entries.summary: ClassiCube is a from-scratch C client that recreates Minecraft Classic multiplayer and single-player modes on modern desktops, phones, browsers, and several niche operating systems. The readme stresses clean-room design, optional visual enhancements, and downloads hosted on classicube.net rather than modern Minecraft services.
features: Run single-player Classic maps or join LAN and ClassiCube.net servers from one launcher.
Choose enhanced rendering options such as custom blocks and environment colors documented in the readme.
Install nightly and stable builds for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, and browser targets linked on classicube.net.
Compile ports for BSD, Solaris, consoles, and other platforms listed in the supported-systems section.
Read the BSD-style license before reusing the CCicon artwork bundled with the repository.
entries.insight: ClassiCube keeps a very specific slice of early Minecraft alive with honest limits—no survival accounts or modern servers—while staying portable enough to run in a browser tab or on retro hardware.

asset.attribution: ClassiCube icon from the official repository. BSD-style license; image used unmodified.

entries.name: OpenJazz
entries.summary: OpenJazz is a GPL-licensed reimplementation of the classic Jazz Jackrabbit engine that runs on desktops, homebrew ports, and a browser build when you supply original game data. The readme documents decades of community ports plus multiplayer experiments added since the project moved to GitHub.
features: Play shareware and full Jazz Jackrabbit data after pointing OpenJazz at original game files.
Build native clients for Windows, Linux, macOS, and numerous homebrew platforms listed in the readme.
Launch the Emscripten web port linked from the repository for browser play with your own data.
Extend the engine with community fixes while keeping GPLv2 licensing documented in licenses.txt.
Use the bundled OpenJazz.png icon under the same GPL terms when crediting upstream artwork.
entries.insight: OpenJazz is a patient fan-engine project: it chases faithful Jazz Jackrabbit behaviour across odd platforms instead of chasing modern store trends, which makes it a fun pick for retro PC collectors.

asset.attribution: OpenJazz icon from the official repository. GPL-2.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

entries.name: GemRB
entries.summary: GemRB is an open-source reimplementation of BioWare’s Infinity Engine used by Baldur’s Gate, Icewind Dale, and Planescape: Torment. The readme and gemrb.org explain that you need legally obtained original game data—or the bundled trivial demo—to see content beyond the sample scenario.
features: Run Infinity Engine RPGs with cleaner modding hooks than the original executables.
Install original PC game data via WINE, installers, or extraction tools documented on gemrb.org.
Try the included trivial demo when you do not yet have full game archives.
Build on Linux, Windows, macOS, and community ports including Android listed in the readme.
Reuse the GemRB logo under GPL terms with attribution to the artwork folder in the repository.
entries.insight: GemRB matters because it keeps isometric RPG classics moddable on modern systems while stating plainly that players must supply original discs or GOG installs—no hidden piracy hand-waving.

asset.attribution: GemRB logo from the official artwork directory. GPL-2.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

Readme: Colonization clone scope and downloads

entries.name: FreeCol
entries.summary: FreeCol is a GPL turn-based strategy game that recreates Sid Meier’s Colonization with an isometric map, multiplayer support, and weekly binary releases for Windows, macOS, and Linux. The readme on GitHub and freecol.org describe incremental work toward a faithful clone plus future 2.0 features.
features: Guide colonists from Europe to independence with trade, founding fathers, and combat systems inspired by Colonization.
Download weekly installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux linked from GitHub releases.
Build from source with Java 11 and Ant as documented in the repository README.
Report bugs and suggest improvements through the SourceForge trackers referenced on freecol.org.
Use the in-repository freecol.png logo under GPL terms noted in the project LICENSE file.
entries.insight: FreeCol is a slow-burn strategy revival: its community still ships cross-platform installers while keeping the rules close to the 1994 original, which suits players who want transparent open-source colonization rather than a reboot.

asset.attribution: FreeCol logo from the official data directory. GPL-2.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

entries.name: NXEngine-evo
entries.summary: NXEngine-evo modernizes the Cave Story engine with SDL2, widescreen resolutions, localization, and bug fixes while remaining a GPL engine port you compile or download from GitHub releases. The readme lists Switch and Vita ports plus build wikis for desktop platforms.
features: Play Cave Story data with widescreen support up to Full HD called out in the readme.
Download prebuilt releases or follow Linux, macOS, and Windows build wikis linked from GitHub.
Enable localization packs, custom soundtracks, and early mod hooks documented upstream.
Benefit from refactored code and gameplay bug fixes compared with legacy NXEngine builds.
Credit the Vita icon asset under GPL-3.0 terms when reusing artwork from the repository.
entries.insight: NXEngine-evo shows how a niche fan engine can add QoL features—widescreen, translations, gamepad rumble—without pretending to replace the original Cave Story commercial release.

asset.attribution: NXEngine-evo icon from official platform packaging assets. GPL-3.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Andor's Trail
entries.summary: Andor's Trail is a GPLv2 roguelike RPG on Android about uncovering what happened to your village and missing brother. The readme links to Google Play, community forums, and quest-driven dungeon crawling with equipment and experience progression.
features: Follow a story-driven campaign with quests, hidden treasure, and tactical combat on Android.
Install the free build from the Google Play listing referenced in the official readme.
Discuss gameplay and contribute through the forums linked from the repository readme.
Build from source using the AndorsTrail Android project in the GitHub repository.
Reuse the launcher icon under GPL-2.0 terms with attribution to the drawable asset path.
entries.insight: Andor's Trail is a rare fully open mobile RPG with a coherent story arc—worth a look if you want offline fantasy crawling without gacha mechanics or account lock-in.

asset.attribution: Andor's Trail launcher icon from the official Android resources. GPL-2.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

entries.name: OpenClonk
entries.summary: OpenClonk is a free multiplayer action game where small humanoids mine, build, and fight in physics-driven scenarios. The GitHub readme documents CMake builds for Windows, Linux, and macOS, while openclonk.org hosts installers and community leagues.
features: Control clonks in fast scenarios with mining, combat, and user-created missions.
Download installers for Windows, Linux, and macOS from openclonk.org.
Build from source with CMake and the dependency list in the repository readme.
Join forums, leagues, and bug trackers linked from the official website.
Use the wide header logo under ISC terms from the COPYING file with attribution to The OpenClonk Team.
entries.insight: OpenClonk mixes Worms-like chaos with settlement tools and a lively league scene—an underrated European open-source sandbox worth discovering if you miss couch-competitive physics games.

asset.attribution: OpenClonk header logo from openclonk.org. ISC license per COPYING; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Aurora Store
entries.summary: Aurora Store is a GPLv3 client that lets you search, inspect, and download apps from Google Play using your own account or an anonymous session. The readme documents Exodus and Plexus privacy integrations, spoofing controls, and limitations around paid titles.
features: Browse Play Store listings with Material 3 UI while downloading APKs through your Google account.
Review tracker reports via integrated Exodus Privacy and Plexus compatibility scores.
Install from F-Droid using the badge linked in the official readme.
Blacklist unwanted updates and fetch older APK builds when Google still hosts them.
Read documented limitations on paid apps and Play Asset Delivery before relying on Aurora for purchases.
entries.insight: Aurora Store is transparent about being an unofficial Play front-end—useful for power users who want FOSS tooling and privacy labels without pretending Google endorses the client.

asset.attribution: Aurora Store launcher icon from fastlane metadata. GPL-3.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Mihon
entries.summary: Mihon is an Apache-licensed Android reader for manga, webtoons, and comics with local libraries, tracker sync, and customizable viewers. The readme highlights stable and beta builds on mihon.app plus integrations with MAL, AniList, Kitsu, and other trackers.
features: Organize series with categories, dark/light themes, and scheduled library updates.
Read through multiple viewer modes with configurable directions and controls.
Sync progress to MangaBaka, MyAnimeList, AniList, Kitsu, and other trackers listed in the readme.
Create local backups or store them in your preferred cloud provider.
Download stable or beta APKs from mihon.app badges linked in the repository readme.
entries.insight: Mihon carries the Tachiyomi spirit forward with above-board Apache licensing and a polished site—handy if you want offline comics reading with tracker sync and no proprietary store lock-in.

asset.attribution: Mihon logo from the official repository assets. Apache-2.0; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Firefox for Android
entries.summary: Firefox for Android (Fenix) is Mozilla’s GeckoView-based mobile browser built on Android Components. The readme links to Google Play, Matrix support channels, and contribution guides for the fully open browser replacing legacy Firefox for Android.
features: Browse with Mozilla’s Gecko engine and Android Components instead of the system WebView.
Install from the Google Play badge embedded in the official GitHub readme.
Use privacy and sync features documented across Mozilla’s Fenix wiki and support sites.
Contribute via GitHub issues following Mozilla’s community participation guidelines.
Reuse the launcher icon under MPL-2.0 terms from the repository mipmap asset.
entries.insight: Firefox for Android remains the flagship open mobile browser from Mozilla—worth revisiting if you want Gecko’s tracking protections on Android without a Chromium-only stack.

asset.attribution: Firefox for Android launcher icon from the Fenix repository. MPL-2.0; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Wikimedia Commons
entries.summary: The Wikimedia Commons Android app uploads photos from your device to Wikimedia Commons with categorization helpers and community documentation. The readme links to Google Play, F-Droid, and extensive contributor docs maintained by volunteers.
features: Upload pictures from Android phones and tablets directly to Wikimedia Commons.
Install via Google Play or F-Droid badges referenced in the official readme.
Follow user and developer documentation linked from the Commons app docs site.
Collaborate through GitHub issues and translation workflows noted in the repository.
Reuse the launcher icon under the project Apache license with attribution to Wikimedia volunteers.
entries.insight: This app turns everyday photos into freely licensed Commons media—a practical Android tool for travelers who want their shots to outlive proprietary camera rolls.

asset.attribution: Wikimedia Commons app icon from the official repository. Apache-2.0; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Nextcloud
entries.summary: The official Nextcloud Android client syncs files, photos, and notifications with self-hosted Nextcloud servers. The readme advertises Google Play, F-Droid, and Obtainium install routes under AGPL-3.0 licensing with REUSE metadata.
features: Connect to your self-hosted Nextcloud for files, sharing, and auto-upload workflows.
Install from Google Play, F-Droid, or Obtainium badges linked in the repository readme.
Review AGPL-3.0 licensing and REUSE compliance badges in the project README.
Follow Nextcloud’s issue tracker and contribution guides for Android-specific fixes.
Reuse the launcher icon under AGPL-3.0 terms from the official mipmap asset.
entries.insight: Nextcloud’s Android app is the missing piece for many homelab setups—offline-friendly syncing without surrendering files to a proprietary cloud dashboard.

asset.attribution: Nextcloud Android launcher icon from the official repository. AGPL-3.0-or-later; image used unmodified.

entries.name: Open Camera
entries.summary: Open Camera is a feature-rich Android camera app from the almalence GitHub mirror with manual controls, scene modes, and plugins. The readme describes it as a multi-functional camera application, with distribution on Google Play and F-Droid under the net.sourceforge.opencamera package.
features: Shoot photos and video with manual exposure, focus, and scene controls on Android.
Install from the Google Play listing tied to net.sourceforge.opencamera.
Grab builds from F-Droid when you prefer fully open distribution mirrors.
Extend capture with plugins referenced in the project’s resource tree.
Reuse the hdpi icon asset from the repository when providing GPL/BSD attribution noted upstream.
entries.insight: Open Camera is a dependable replacement for stock camera apps—lightweight, offline-friendly, and maintained openly long after many OEM cameras locked features behind proprietary skins.

asset.attribution: Open Camera icon from the official repository drawable assets. GPL-3.0-or-later per LICENSE; image used unmodified.

entries.name: OctoDroid
entries.summary: OctoDroid (gh4a) is an open-source GitHub client for Android covering repositories, issues, pull requests, gists, and notifications. The readme embeds an F-Droid badge for com.gh4a and documents OAuth setup for building from source.
features: Browse repositories, commits, and file trees with syntax-highlighted diffs on Android.
Manage issues and pull requests including comments, labels, and milestones.
Explore trending projects and GitHub timelines from the Explore section.
Install from F-Droid using the badge linked in the official readme.
Register a GitHub OAuth application with callback gh4a://oauth when building custom builds.
entries.insight: OctoDroid is still one of the most complete open GitHub clients on Android—handy for maintainers who want issue triage on the go without a proprietary wrapper.

asset.attribution: OctoDroid mascot icon from the official repository. Apache-2.0; image used unmodified.
